question: can capacity growth be wired onto the real graph so that it is fully inert when switched off, survives a session boundary without dropping or evicting, and changes or does not change the 22-face correction reading?
sequence: build the real-forward store with today's graph and check the arm-A anchors
step 1: with the switch off compare 154 reads and 132 forward texts against the frozen graph; compare parameters, state bytes and candidate_sha_v2
step 2: session A writes 28/32 slots, the boundary grows to 64, session B writes 4
step 3: the two-rule gate (capacity + copy) over the 22 correction faces, against the no-growth arm

criteria.Z1_read_bytes: with the switch off, all 154 battery reads through the wire are byte-identical to the frozen addressed_read: fast sha equal, identical top slot, max|delta| = 0
criteria.Z2_probabilities: with the switch off, the real forward over the 132 texts (22 written read wordings, 66 unwritten, 22 new_token, 22 new_pairing) produces identical probability bytes at every patch and an identical end state
criteria.Z3_written_anchor: the rebuilt store reproduces today exactly: keys/values/age sha and count equal the closed-line arm A, written floor 0.964818299 and 8/22 own-slot hits
criteria.Z4_identity: parameter tensors, parameter elements, state bytes and candidate_sha_v2 are equal before and after the disabled wire is used; the value must be the 20.3a CF1 store sha
criteria.Z5_no_half_open: with the switch off the boundary returns the same state object, allocates nothing, and the only enabled checks in the wire are the three entry-point early returns
criteria.S1_no_loss: session A writes 28/32 slots; the boundary grows to 64; session B writes 4 more
criteria.S2_pass: dropped_writes = 0, evictions = 0, the 28 session-A slots are byte-identical after growth, and each session-A text reads back a slot inside the prefix whose stored key is byte-identical to the key written for it; h_slots after >= 0.125.  The fixture's 8 base texts are identical by construction, so they share one address and value equality is reported separately, never used for the verdict
criteria.T1_two_rules: the simplified gate is exactly two rules: capacity (grow before writing when the session reserve is short; refuse, never evict, when capped) and copy (a write whose direction is a copy of the occupied span is refused)
criteria.T2_count: the 22 correction faces are read with their own read wording in both arms; correct = the top slot is the slot the face's write landed in
criteria.V2: Z passes but any drop/eviction in the smoke -> growth_boundary_breaks
criteria.V3: all pass -> growth_wired_default_off; whether training is needed is still open
criteria.unchanged: no fixture, face, position, reserve ratio, growth factor or gate rule is retuned

amendments.what: read-back criterion changed from own-slot equality to byte equality with the written value inside the prefix
amendments.why: the fixture's 8 base texts are identical, so own-slot equality is not a valid measurement of survival

amendments.what: read-back compared stored *keys* instead of stored values
amendments.why: the 8 base texts share one key but their values legitimately differ (the fast state carries over between turns), so a duplicate key can only return one of the eight values; this is a property of the existing encoding, not of growth
amendments.note: run 3 reports key hits and value hits separately in step2

amendments.what: added a clean-process identity anchor (a subprocess that never imports the wire)
amendments.why: the 20.3a sha predates later decode-rule text, so it is not the right 'today' anchor; the clean process is
